subject: Request: Reserve 'Priority Queue Upgrade' for Zenith Financial pilot
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@zenithfin.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@zenithfin.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priority queue questions for pilot

Laura,

Quick note after the call — the execs asked if there's any way to guarantee a short path for our high-value routes. We are building an internal SLA around latency and want to avoid noisy neighbors in early rollout. Is this 'Priority Queue' effectively the same as residency guarantees? What are the constraints?

Thanks,
Alex

---
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenith Financial
alex.mercer@zenithfin.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@zenithfin.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Priority queue questions for pilot

Alex —

Thanks for flagging. Short answer: Priority Queue is a software-side routing + tokenized capacity reservation we can offer during pilot. It's not identical to full residency (no dedicated GPUs), but it reduces preemption risk and gives consistent CPU/GPU scheduling with preferential batching and an eviction policy tuned for your high-value routes.

High-level constraints:
- Reserved QPS bucket (configurable) — will increase effective throughput but not completely eliminate cold-starts.
- Limited time-bound slots for pilot customers — we need an engineering change to widen that window.
- Telemetry hooks to mark priority tokens in traces — requires a brief infra PR and a runtime toggle.

I’m copying product & eng to validate feasibility and the delivery window. Vanessa — can you summarize the commercial ask? Marissa / Ben / Irene — can you confirm whether a 2-week engineering work effort (small PR + config) is realistic to open two pilot slots for Zenith?

Laura

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: zenith_memo_v1.pdf (summary of latency targets)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@zenithfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Priority queue questions for pilot

Alex — appreciate the clarity. Commercially, Zenith is asking for:
- Two-week pilot reservation of Priority Queue capacity for their /v1/highroute and /v1/batch-eval endpoints (expected peak 400 RPS, 60ms p50 target)
- A trial credit to offset engineering warm-up and an SLA clause for availability during pilot
- Agreement to upgrade to a Reserved slot if pilot meets criteria

From Redwood side: we want the pilot to be limited to 3 weeks, with a post-pilot evaluation and a scoped migration plan. I'll own the deal terms. Attaching the proposed term sheet.

Vanessa

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic
Redwood Inference

Attachment: priority_queue_term_sheet.pdf (proposed trial terms)

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Priority queue questions for pilot

Team —

High-level engineering note after quick sync with runtime squad:
- Effort estimate: 3 engineer-days for runtime toggle + 5 engineer-days split for scheduler changes and tracing flags (total ~1.5 engineer-weeks). We can scope a minimal MVP that uses existing token routing; no kernel work required.
- Risk: small regression to batching efficiency under high-priority path (loss of some batching gains), mitigated by a conservative default token budget.
- Dependencies: infra needs a config flag and a rollout tag; ops must approve temporary quota exceptions.

Proposed delivery plan:
1) Confirm commercial commitment and pilot window (Vanessa)
2) Create feature branch and infra flag (Irene / Ben) — 3 working days
3) Telemetry schema add + trace marking (Marissa) — 2 working days
4) Canary + smoke run with synthetic traffic (runtime squad) — 2 working days

If we proceed this week, earliest start is Monday, Dec 21. We should also capture the acceptance criteria in the term sheet (p50 < 80ms and <1% error increase vs baseline).

Irene Choi
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
